seed: I want to bank a framework I use with every client. I call it the Handoff Ladder. Three rungs: write it down, hand it off, review it weekly. You cannot skip a rung. It exists because delegation falls apart when the handoff has no structure. The owner says "I delegated it" and a week later the work is back on their desk.

reveals: Rung one is write it down: the process leaves your head and becomes a document. Until it is written, you have not delegated, you have just hoped.
Rung two is hand it off: a named owner takes the document and runs it. One owner, not a group.
Rung three is review it weekly: a standing check so the system drifts back into shape instead of back onto your desk.
The rungs are strictly ordered, each one depends on the one before, so the shape is arrows.
It is a process framework. I would tag it delegation and systems.
